friction.what: The dominant element on the capture screen is a large photo-preview panel that can never show a photo. It renders `aspect-[4/3]` (phone) / `sm:aspect-[3/2]` in the wider grid column and contains only a camera glyph and "Add a photo to start"; the moment a photo exists, the app leaves this screen for the review modal.
friction.why_it_hurts: On a phone this is a full screen-height of dead space the salesperson scrolls past every single post, and it makes the screen look like a desktop uploader rather than a one-tap camera tool. It exists only to host the desktop drag-and-drop overlay (lines 273-280), which a phone cannot do.
friction.evidence:
`className="capture-studio-preview table-lit relative flex aspect-[4/3] ... sm:aspect-[3/2]"` with body `

Add a photo to start

` (CameraCapture.tsx:252-285)

friction.what: A mandatory full-screen modal called "Review photo" that offers no edit of any kind — no crop, no rotate, no straighten. Its own description says "Check the framing. The photo is kept at its original size." and the file header admits the component name is vestigial.
friction.why_it_hurts: On mobile this is the SECOND confirmation of the same photo: iOS's camera already asked Retake/Use Photo. It adds a modal and a tap to every post while giving the salesperson nothing they can act on — if the framing is wrong their only option is "Choose another" and start the camera over.
friction.evidence: "Legacy component name retained to avoid changing the app controller. This is the single authoritative photo review surface for every capture source." (lines 42-45); description "Check the framing. The photo is kept at its original size." (line 186); decorative rails commented "echo platform-safe crop guides without applying a crop" (line 270)

friction.what: Three competing footer actions with no hierarchy: "Choose another" (ghost, destructive — discards the capture), "Save original to Photos"/"Download original" (ghost, a filesystem chore), "Use photo" (primary). The two ghosts are styled identically.
friction.why_it_hurts: The one screen whose entire job is "yes, this photo" asks a three-way question, and the file-management option sits between the discard and the continue. Saving a copy to the camera roll is not part of posting and does not belong at the decision point.
friction.evidence: grid `sm:grid-cols-[auto_1fr_auto]` with `variant="ghost"` on both "Choose another" (line 193) and the save button (line 201), `variant="primary"` on "Use photo" (line 225)

friction.what: The review modal's status strip narrates the implementation: "Original ratio retained · working copy max 2048 px", "Backing up original in app…", "Original backed up in app", "Local backup unavailable — use Save original", "Use Save original for your Photos library".
friction.why_it_hurts: Four distinct system states, pixel dimensions, and the phrase "in app" are shown to a salesperson standing next to a customer. It explains the system instead of the task, and one variant is an instruction to go press a different button.
friction.evidence: `Original ratio retained · working copy max 2048 px` (line 289); `"Local backup unavailable — use Save original"` (line 305)

friction.what: HEIC/HEIF failure is a dead end. The message tells the user to change an iPhone camera setting and retake the photo: "This photo is in Apple's HEIC/HEIF format, which this browser cannot read. Take the photo again with 'Most Compatible' format enabled, or use a JPEG/PNG." The ErrorBanner's action looks like a retry but only clears the text.
friction.why_it_hurts: The primary device is an iPhone, the primary source is the camera roll, and HEIC is its default format. The salesperson is sent into iOS Settings mid-job with the customer waiting, and the 'retry' affordance does not retry anything.
friction.evidence: CameraCapture.tsx:74-80; `onRetry={() => { triggerHapticFeedback(); setError(null); }}` (lines 211-214)

friction.what: Photos over 12 MB are rejected outright — "That photo is too large. Choose an image smaller than 12 MB." — even though the very next step downscales everything to 2048 px anyway.
friction.why_it_hurts: The app already has the code to shrink the image (utils/imageUtils.ts:246-330) but asks the salesperson to solve a byte-size problem instead. A modern phone photo (ProRAW, burst, 48 MP) hits this, and the message offers no path forward.
friction.evidence: `const maxSizeInBytes = 12 * 1024 * 1024;` then `setError("That photo is too large. Choose an image smaller than 12 MB.")` (lines 49-52)

friction.what: The three coaching lines that actually help a salesperson frame a compliant delivery photo are desktop-only: the block is `hidden ... sm:block`.
friction.why_it_hurts: "Keep the customer and the vehicle fully in frame." and "Avoid backlight and visible paperwork." are exactly the phone-side guidance that prevents a reshoot and a privacy problem — and they are hidden on the only device where the photo is taken.
friction.evidence: `className="capture-studio-tips mt-6 hidden border-t border-hairline pt-6 sm:block"` (line 244)

friction.what: Capture collects no context about the job. The product has six post categories (deliveries / inventory / service / promotions / community / team) but the first screen only says "Start with a photo" and the progress rail calls the next step "Details".
friction.why_it_hurts: The cheapest moment to know "this is a customer delivery" is when the salesperson opens the app to shoot one — that answer could pre-select the scenario, the platform set, and the photo-release requirement downstream. Instead every post starts context-free and the salesperson re-declares intent on a later screen.

They clear sooner when you log out.", and an unconditional `<Badge variant="success">Backed up</Badge>`.

The "Backed up" badge is hardcoded while the review modal reports four different backup outcomes for the same mechanism — two surfaces telling different stories about one fact.

keep: One review surface for every capture source. Camera, file picker, drag-drop and shelf-reuse all funnel through the same `onImageSelected` → ImageCropModal path, so the app never double-confirms internally — the code comment states the intent: "The global crop/review dialog is the single review surface for every source. Calling it directly avoids two sequential confirmation steps." (CameraCapture.tsx:61-68). Any redesign should keep exactly one confirmation point, not zero and not two.

Device-local original recovery: the untouched original Blob is archived to IndexedDB the instant a photo is selected (useAppController.ts:183-195), surfaced as the Recent originals shelf, capped at 24 records / 3 videos per dealer, TTL 48 h, cleared on logout (utils/creativeStorage.ts:13-15). This is genuine offline/crash insurance on lot Wi-Fi and it costs the happy path nothing.

The working-copy/original split: the app hands the pipeline an EXIF-normalized 2048 px JPEG while "Save original" and the shelf still hold the untouched original Blob (utils/imageUtils.ts:246-330; RecentCaptureShelf.tsx:28-32). Salespeople never lose the real photo.

Privacy posture of the local archive: records deliberately carry no customer names or captions (LocalMediaArchive.tsx:51-55) and the shelf clears on logout — keep this when the storage copy is rewritten.

Honest offline handling: OfflineBanner states "You're offline — your work is saved on this device and sharing resumes when you reconnect." and it is true, not a placebo (components/OfflineBanner.tsx:17-26).

The PWA update prompt never self-activates over in-progress work — the user decides, so a post is never discarded underneath them (PwaUpdatePrompt.tsx:61-67). Given the known stale-build problem, keep both the prompt and the 60 s foreground re-check.
PanelErrorBoundary around the photo-review modal: a crash in review shows a compact inline panel instead of blanking the whole workspace (App.tsx:449).

Cold-cache protection on the critical tap: idle prefetch of the review chunk after login plus the "Opening photo review…" Suspense fallback so picking a photo is never a dead tap (App.tsx:168-198, 454-471).

Back-gesture mapping: the step machine is mirrored into #/step history so the platform Back gesture walks the flow instead of exiting the installed PWA, and it refuses to bypass the RESULT leave-confirmation (hooks/useUrlStepSync.ts).

Camera hygiene in WebcamCapture: streams are torn down on unmount and on camera flip so the camera light never stays on (lines 43-48, 88-95, 128-131), and the shutter refuses to emit a 0×0 JPEG before the first frame (lines 141-143).

Accessible dialog mechanics in ui/Modal: focus moved in on open, restored to the trigger on close, a real Tab trap, Escape to close, body-scroll lock — and it deliberately does not steal focus that a fast user already moved (Modal.tsx:52-105).
Recoverable capture errors stay inline rather than unmounting the studio, so the two capture buttons remain reachable (CameraCapture.tsx:205-217).

happy_path.scenario: A salesperson on an iPhone, already signed in, shoots a customer-delivery photo and gets it into the Details step so it can go to Facebook.
happy_path.narrative: She lands on the capture screen, which reads "Step 1 of 3 · Photo" above a heading that says "Start with a photo" and a line of reassurance — "Take a new photo or choose one from your device. You'll review it before anything is created." Below the two buttons sits a large empty panel showing a camera icon and "Add a photo to start", a preview frame that will never show her a photo, and beneath that a strip headed "Recent originals" explaining that "Private rescue copies on this device" last "up to 48 hours" — none of which she needs right now. She taps "Take photo" (tap 1), the phone's own camera opens, she presses the shutter (tap 2) and then iOS's own "Use Photo" (tap 3). The app shows "Preparing your photo…" over the empty panel, then a modal slides up titled "Review photo" with the description "Check the framing. The photo is kept at its original size." — so she is confirming the same photo a second time, and there is nothing here she can actually adjust. Under the image a status line reads "Original ratio retained · working copy max 2048 px" next to "Backing up original in app…", and the footer offers her three choices: "Choose another", "Save original to Photos", and the one she wants, "Use photo". She taps "Use photo" (tap 4); the button reads "Preparing photo" for a beat and the app moves her to Details. happy_path.scenario: Salesperson on a phone, dealer without approval or brand mode, Customer Delivery photo with Facebook Feed as the only destination, photo release saved, no compliance locks. Starts when generation completes and ends when they leave the result for a new photo.
happy_path.narrative: Once generation finishes, the phone opens the dark publish studio. The header shows 'Facebook Feed' with 'Posting as {name}' and 'Photo · 4:5 · 1080×1350', and the status card goes from 'Preparing' to 'Ready — File ready. Caption is included when you share.' The bottom bar offers a filled 'Save', an outline 'Share' and 'Copy'. They tap Share (1), and a 'Share exact output' modal opens explaining 'Media prepares now, before you press Share now…'. It then shows 'Facebook is ready' with 'Copy caption' and 'Share now'. They tap 'Share now' (2), the iOS share sheet opens with the photo and the caption is copied silently, and they pick the Facebook app (3) to paste and post outside the PWA. Back in the app, the modal shows 'Media sent to the share sheet. The caption is ready to paste in the destination app.' and a 5-step 'Finish in the Facebook app' checklist. There is no 'posted' confirmation, so they close it (4). They tap the back arrow for a new photo (5) and are warned 'Create another post? — This result is not fully preserved yet', even though they just shared it, so they tap the red 'Discard and continue' (6).

variants.entry: Two doors. (1) Capture screen: a "Creation mode" segmented toggle, "Photo post" | "Vehicle walkaround", appears only when the build flag VITE_WALKAROUND_STUDIO_ENABLED=true (components/MainContent.tsx:350-398, default "photo" at :173-175). (2) Result/publish screen (components/PostResult.tsx): a creative tile row with Video, Fun mode and Schedule, plus a "More" disclosure (:4786-4908). In brand mode the same tiles read "Add video", "Playful" and "Studio tools". The "More" panel holds Export sizes, Regenerate image, Edit image, Regenerate caption, Edit text and "3 text ideas" (:4971-5125). Resumable walkaround uploads: per-file persisted progress with chunk resume, the project id restored after reload, the server as source of truth, and "You can leave this screen".

Video Director duplicate-spend guards: isSubmitting disables styles, plus a synchronous videoGenerationActiveRef (PostResult.tsx:555). Exact-delivery pinning ("Exact output pinned") keeps platform video files at their native ratio.

"Playful" applies the one dealer-chosen style and keeps the house master beside it (renderPlayfulPair). Retries are one-shot. Review lock: Video and Fun mode are blocked after review ("This reviewed creative must stay unchanged. Start a new post to create a video."), and remix tools need the original capture with a clear message on reopened History.

happy_path.scenario: A salesperson posts a customer-delivery photo to Facebook. Within the variants area this is the default path: optional modes are skipped (legacy dealership, walkaround flag on or off).
happy_path.narrative: On Capture, if the walkaround build flag is on, the salesperson first sees a "Photo post" | "Vehicle walkaround" toggle. It already defaults to "Photo post", so no tap is needed and they carry on with the photo. On the result screen the variant surfaces are all optional. A tile row offers "Video", "Fun mode" and "Schedule", plus a "More" disclosure (six tools: Export sizes, Regenerate image, Edit image, Regenerate caption, Edit text, 3 text ideas). For Facebook, the salesperson ignores all of it and shares, so the variants area adds 0 taps, 0 screens, 0 modals and 0 typed fields. The cost is attention: at equal visual weight, these tiles compete with the share action. If they are tempted by "Video" (legacy), the minimum is 2 taps and 1 modal ("Creator video"), facing "Format for", "Video quality", "Aspect ratio", "Sound" and "Length" before 8 "★ Pro" styles, and the first style tap immediately starts a paid render. If they try "Fun mode", the minimum is 3 taps and 1 modal (tile, style, "Generate style") among 12 top picks such as "Pixar", "LEGO" and "GTA". In brand mode the same detours drop to 1 tap and no modal ("Add video" / "Playful").

happy_path.scenario: (a) Salesperson checks a customer-delivery post in My work and reopens it; (b) manager approves one pending post; (c) manager adds a new salesperson and hands out the code. Totals are summed; per-job split: (a) 2 taps, 1 modal, 0 typed; (b) 2 taps + 1 typed name; (c) 5 taps + 1 typed name.
happy_path.narrative: (a) After publishing, the salesperson taps the unlabeled history icon in the header ("Open my work") and gets a full-screen "My work" modal. It reads "Reopen prior creatives, captions, and customer posts without regenerating.", then a second heading "My posts" with a "{n} visible · {n} posts loaded · archive up to date" line, sometimes a "Recent media on this device" strip, a search box, and five filter chips. On the phone card they see a "pending" or "rejected" badge. If it was rejected the reason is not shown on mobile, so they tap Open and land on the result studio with the toast "Creative reopened — share or export without regenerating." (b) The manager signs in with their code and lands on "Manager dashboard". If brand voice or color is unset, a 9-step "Set up {dealer}" card sits on top until they tap Later. They scroll past the "Salesperson leaderboard" to "Pending Approvals", tap the "Reviewing as (manager name — required to approve)" field, and type their own name, since the app does not prefill it. They read the creative, the "Submitted caption", destination captions, and "Required disclosures", then tap Approve. The card vanishes with no confirmation, and the Post history below still says pending. (c) The manager taps the Team tab, taps "Add salesperson", types "Sarah Chen", and taps Add (Enter does not submit). A card appears: "Sarah Chen's access code is ready" / "Copy this one-time access code and share it privately." They tap Copy, send the code privately outside the app, and tap "Mark as shared", which turns the row badge from "Code to share" to "Code set".
